Maya (PM): Quick sync — proposing a staged rollout plan for smart-routing v2 (feature flags + canaries + A/B + fallback). Aim: reduce tail latency and lower cost without regressions. Thoughts?

Jordan (Eng): +1. We should gate by flag at the request-router layer and do traffic-splitting at the LB. Canary traffic idea: start 5% on us-west, then 25%, 50% before full.

Simon (SRE): Agree. Also need synthetic load and golden traces in canary to verify correctness. We should set automated alerting on error_rate and p95 latency for the canary.

Alice (ML): For A/B, we need an eval harness feeding our golden prompt set and a small human eval for quality-sensitive customers. Metrics: exact-match on key prompts, safety checks, and perplexity drift.

Maya (PM): Proposed launch criteria (must pass all): 1) canary error_rate delta <= 1.5% absolute; 2) p95 latency increase <= 10ms; 3) quality regression on golden set <= 0.7% (or manual signoff); 4) cost/unit delta <= +20%. If any fail, roll back.

Jordan (Eng): For rollout controls I'll add a feature-flag entry in LaunchDarkly and a runtime toggle in infra. Example flag plan:
```
flag: smart-routing-v2
variants: off, canary, on
canary: 5% us-west only
rollout: 5 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100
metrics: latency_p50, latency_p95, error_rate, model_quality_score
```
We can short-circuit to `off` automatically via the operator script.

Simon (SRE): Fallback policy: if canary error_rate > 1.5% for 5m OR p95 increase > 25ms for 5m then auto-fallback to routing-v1 for canary pool. Also add a manual abort path. Need runbook entries.

deploy-bot: deploy started for smart-routing-v2 canary @ 2024-04-23T16:05:12Z :rocket:

Ravi (CS): Heads up — two enterprise customers on dedicated capacity asked for explicit opt-in before we switch their traffic. We should exclude dedicated pools unless they opt-in.

Alice (ML): For the A/B experiment sample size: to detect a 0.7% quality delta with 80% power we need ~60k evals across cohorts; that maps to ~48 hours at 5% traffic for our production qps. Recommend 48-hour canary with progressive ramp and continuous eval.

Jordan (Eng): Implementation steps (rough):
- config flag + LB routing rules
- canary service subset (us-west instances)
- deploy model bundle + routing logic behind flag
- enable flag at 5% with synthetic traffic and monitoring
- ramp per metrics and run A/B eval tasks
- finalize and flip global flag
Will post PRs for infra + runtime today.

Simon (SRE): Monitoring checklist: dashboards for canary vs baseline, synthetic traces, error budget burn, rollback automation test, alert runbook links. I'll own dashboards + automation.

Maya (PM): Risks: model-quality regressions, increased cost, unforeseen cache misses causing latency spikes. Mitigations: golden set eval, temporary soft-rate-limit, KV cache warm-up script.

Jordan (Eng): Cache warm-up note: we should prefill KV for canary pool using recent popular prefixes. Will add a small job to pre-warm on deploy.

Maya (PM): Timeline: start canary Thursday EOD, 48-72h window, decision meeting Friday + 1 day. Communication: release notes, customer emails for enterprise opt-in, internal changelog.

Ravi (CS): I'll draft the enterprise opt-in template and send to legal for compliance wording.

Maya (PM): Action items: Jordan - infra PR + flag config; Simon - dashboards + rollback automation; Alice - eval harness + human eval plan; Ravi - enterprise comms. Meet again after first 24h of canary. :thumbsup:
